name: ADC102S021CIMMX_NOPB
title: 10-bit, two-input serial ADC specified from 50 ksps to 200 ksps
summary: The ADC102S021 is a 10-bit successive-approximation converter with a track-and-hold and a two-way input multiplexer (IN1, IN2), read through a four-wire serial port that works with SPI, QSPI, MICROWIRE and many DSP ports. Its performance is guaranteed across sample rates from 50 ksps to 200 ksps. It runs from one 2.7 V to 5.25 V supply, which is also its reference, and powers down whenever CS is high. The package is an 8-lead VSSOP, rated from −40 °C to +85 °C.
key_figures: 1.94 mW typ at 3.6 V, 6.9 mW typ at 5.25 V

notes: The orderable versions differ in reel quantity (1000 or 3500) and lead finish; all are VSSOP (DGK), 8 pins, −40 °C to 85 °C.

pins.name: CS
pins.function: Chip select, active low. A falling edge starts a conversion; the part keeps converting for as long as the pin stays low, and is powered down while it is high.

pins.name: VA
pins.function: Supply, +2.7 V to +5.25 V, and the conversion reference. Feed it from a quiet source and decouple it to GND with 1 µF plus a 0.1 µF monolithic capacitor, both within 1 cm of the pin.

pins.name: IN2
pins.function: Analog input 2; range 0 V to VA.

pins.name: IN1
pins.function: Analog input 1; range 0 V to VA. Selected by default after power-up.

pins.name: DIN
pins.function: Serial data into the control register, taken on SCLK rising edges.

pins.name: DOUT
pins.function: Serial conversion result, shifted out on SCLK falling edges; high impedance while CS is high.

pins.name: SCLK
pins.function: Serial clock. It times both the conversion itself and the data transfer.

circuits.title: Typical application circuit
circuits.description: An LP2950 low-dropout regulator turns a 5 V rail into the converter's supply, which is also its reference. The regulator input has 1 µF and 0.1 µF to ground; its output, the VA node, has a 1 µF tantalum and a 0.1 µF placed near the converter. A microprocessor or DSP drives SCLK, CS and DIN and reads DOUT. IN1 and IN2 take the two analog signals.
notes: Supply noise reaches the result directly, since VA is the reference: give the converter its own linear regulator or enough decoupling from other loads; a precision reference can also power it, given its low current.

circuits.title: Timing test circuit
circuits.description: Load used to measure the output timing. The output pin sees 50 pF to ground and a diode bridge whose far corner sits at 1.6 V; a 200 µA source into the top corner (IOL) and a 200 µA sink from the bottom corner (IOH) set the current the pin must sink or source.

operation.text: A charge-redistribution DAC, a comparator and a sampling capacitor form the SAR. In track mode switch SW1 links the sampling capacitor through the multiplexer to the chosen input and SW2 balances the comparator; this lasts the first three SCLK cycles after CS falls. In hold mode SW1 grounds the capacitor, SW2 unbalances the comparator, and the logic adds charge steps until the comparator balances; the DAC code is then the result. Hold runs from SCLK cycle 4 to 16.

A frame runs from CS falling to CS rising and must hold a whole multiple of 16 rising SCLK edges. Each 16 clocks give one conversion: the result leaves DOUT MSB first from the 5th falling edge, while the control word for the next conversion enters DIN on the first 8 rising edges. DOUT is high impedance whenever CS is high, so CS also acts as the output enable.
With CS held low the part keeps converting. For N an integer, it goes back to track on the SCLK falling edge after rising edge N×16 and to hold on falling edge N×16+4.

SCLK is gated off inside while CS is high. If SCLK rests low, CS falling makes an internal falling edge that counts as the first one and starts tracking. If SCLK rests high, tracking starts at the first real falling edge after CS falls. Breaking tCSU or tCLH can shift the first DIN capture one clock later.
Every conversion clocks in the address of the channel for the following conversion (ADD2..ADD0 in bits 5..3). ADD1 must stay 0; with it set, DOUT is indeterminate.
No start-up delay or dummy conversion is needed: the first conversion after power-up is a full one, and it reads IN1.
Output coding is straight binary. One LSB is VA/1024; code transitions sit midway between whole LSB values, the first at VA/2048.

Each input has ESD diodes D1 and D2 to VA and GND, about 3 pF of pin capacitance (C1), about 500 Ω of multiplexer and track/hold switch resistance (R1) and a sampling capacitor (C2) of about 30 pF. Keep inputs within VA + 300 mV and GND − 300 mV; beyond that the diodes conduct and conversion can go wrong, so they must not be used as clamps. A low-impedance source avoids distortion from charging the sampling capacitor, which matters most with AC signals; a band-pass or low-pass filter ahead of the input cuts harmonics and noise.
DOUT swings no higher than VA. The digital inputs do not latch up, and SCLK, CS and DIN may be driven before VA is applied, though this is not recommended.

The part is fully powered while CS is low and fully powered down while CS is high. It also powers down by itself between the 16th falling edge of one conversion and the first falling edge of the next. Running SCLK at 3.2 MHz and converting less often trades throughput for power.

Charging the DOUT load draws current pulses from VA, and discharging it dumps current into the resistive substrate; both can lower SNR and SINAD, more so with a larger load. Keep the load capacitance small; above 50 pF, put a 100 Ω resistor in series with DOUT, as near the pin as possible.
VA needs 1 µF and a 0.1 µF monolithic capacitor to GND, both within 1 cm of the pin, from a quiet 2.7 V to 5.25 V source.
ESD protection is limited; store the parts with leads shorted or in conductive foam.
